message.reasoning_content:
I am reviewing the VP's draft payment decision to identify errors.

I am applying strict criteria to judge the draft. I will only object to concrete problems: ignored findings, unsupported reasons, or approvals that conflict with a reject-severity finding or high risk memo. Rejections must be backed by a reject-severity finding or a high risk memo; otherwise they are invalid.

The invoice total is $9,975, below the $10,000 threshold. Finding F1 is near-threshold and informational. I am checking whether the draft addresses this finding.

Finding F3 is the only reject-severity finding. It confirms this invoice duplicates a paid invoice from the same vendor. The draft correctly rejects it based on that finding. The risk memo is low and all findings are addressed. The total is under $10,000, so the threshold rule does not apply. The draft appears sound.

The risk memo cites a line reading "formerly FastShip Ltd.", but the invoice contains no such text. The vendor master record shows FastShip Ltd. as an alias for QuickShip Distributers, yet the invoice uses the canonical name. This discrepancy is a concrete factual error.

The draft is sound. The risk memo discrepancy does not undermine the rejection, and all findings are correctly addressed.
